plan.melodySummary: The famous theme migrates through the ensemble in even six-measure spans: Violin 1 opens espressivo, hands off to warm Clarinet, then French Horn, back to Violin 1 for the climactic variation, down to the singing Cello, and finally reunites in Violin 1 for the cadence. Dynamics trace a Romantic arc from a tender !p! opening, swelling through hairpins to a radiant !ff! high point around mm.19-24, then settling back to a glowing !mf! resolution.

sections.label: Phrase A — Statement
sections.notes: Sing the theme espressivo at !p!, dolce, with a gentle hairpin crescendo into m.4 and slight lingering on the E in m.4; all other voices stay softer than !p! underneath.

sections.label: Phrase B — Warm Restatement
sections.notes: Take the melody at !mp! with a woody, singing tone; Violin 1 weaves a chromatic descant above while accompaniment keeps flowing arpeggios beneath, all balanced below the clarinet.

sections.label: Phrase C — Horn Nobilmente
sections.notes: State the theme nobilmente at !mf!, broadening at the upper turn in mm.17-18 with a hairpin; strings shimmer in repeated-chord tremolo kept softer than the horn.

sections.label: Phrase D — Full Climax
sections.notes: The high point: play at !f! rising to !ff! by m.24, brilliant and impassioned with full vibrato; horn doubles an octave-lower countermelody, all inner voices rich but under the melody.

sections.label: Phrase E — Cello Cantabile
sections.notes: Sing the melody in the tenor register at !mf!, molto espressivo, easing back with a diminuendo through m.30; clarinet takes the low bass line so the cello can soar, all others softer.

sections.label: Coda — Cadence
sections.notes: Play the final cadence at !mf! with a warm ritard-feel on the sustained D, glowing and resolved; harmony swells to meet the melody then settles, never exceeding it.

Violin 1.instruction: Lead espressivo with singing legato and generous vibrato; shape every phrase with !p!→!f!→!p! hairpins, provide chromatic descants when not carrying the tune, and always project above accompaniment when leading.

Violin 2.instruction: Supply flowing arpeggios and gently repeated inner-voice chords with chromatic suspensions resolving downward; stay dynamically beneath whichever instrument holds the melody, breathing with short rests at phrase ends.

Clarinet.instruction: When leading, sing with a warm woody cantabile at !mp!; elsewhere provide legato inner harmony or a soft bass in mm.25-30, always subordinate in dynamic to the melody carrier.

French Horn.instruction: Play nobilmente when carrying the theme at !mf!; otherwise sustain rich horn pedal harmonies and octave-lower countermelodies at the climax, tucked beneath the lead voice.

Cello.instruction: Provide a flowing, walking arpeggiated bass with expressive rubato under other sections; when carrying the melody in mm.25-30, sing molto espressivo in the tenor range at !mf! above the transferred bass.
